# Classification marking fixtures

Generated by `gen.py` (Python 3 stdlib, run as `python3 -I gen.py`). Regenerating produces identical bytes.

Fixed values:

- Tenant / site id: `72f988bf-86f1-41af-91ab-2d7cd011db47`
- MIP label "Confidential": `9fbde396-1a24-4c79-8edf-9254a0f35055`
- MIP label "Internal": `87ba5c36-b7cf-4793-bbc2-bd5b3a9f95ca`
- MIP label "Highly Confidential" (deliberately unmapped in tests): `f42aa342-8706-4288-bd11-ebb85995028c`

Values chosen by the generator (not fixed by the brief):

- `_ActionId` in every MSIP custom property: `5d1c2a7e-0b3f-4e8a-9c6d-2f7b1a4e8d90`
- ODT `BusinessAuthorizationCategory:Identifier`: `confidential`; `PolicyAuthority:Name`: `Example Policy Authority`

Property names below abbreviate the GUID: `MSIP_Label_<guid>_Enabled` means `MSIP_Label_9fbde396-1a24-4c79-8edf-9254a0f35055_Enabled` for Confidential, and so on.

| File | Format | Where the marking sits | Marked value | Expected reader result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `mip_confidential.docx` | DOCX (OOXML) | `docProps/custom.xml`, `MSIP_Label_<guid>_*` custom properties (`Name`=Confidential, `SiteId`, `Method`=Standard, `Enabled`=true) | Label Confidential, GUID `9fbde396-1a24-4c79-8edf-9254a0f35055` | Label `Confidential` (GUID `9fbde396-1a24-4c79-8edf-9254a0f35055`) |
| `labelinfo_internal.docx` | DOCX (OOXML) | `docMetadata/LabelInfo.xml`, `clbl:label id="{87ba5c36-...}"` (relationship type `classificationlabels` in `_rels/.rels`) | Label Internal, GUID `87ba5c36-b7cf-4793-bbc2-bd5b3a9f95ca` | Label GUID `87ba5c36-b7cf-4793-bbc2-bd5b3a9f95ca`, mapped to `Internal`. The part carries no name, so the name comes from the mapping |
| `mip_unmapped.docx` | DOCX (OOXML) | `docProps/custom.xml`, `MSIP_Label_<guid>_*` with `Name`=Highly Confidential | Label Highly Confidential, GUID `f42aa342-8706-4288-bd11-ebb85995028c` | Unmapped label: GUID `f42aa342-8706-4288-bd11-ebb85995028c` with no catalog classification. Do not guess one |
| `unlabelled.docx` | DOCX (OOXML) | No label part at all | None | No label (`None`) |
| `mip_confidential.xlsx` | XLSX (OOXML) | `docProps/custom.xml`, same `MSIP_Label_<guid>_*` properties as the DOCX | Label Confidential, GUID `9fbde396-1a24-4c79-8edf-9254a0f35055` | Label `Confidential` (GUID `9fbde396-1a24-4c79-8edf-9254a0f35055`) |
| `mip_internal.pdf` | PDF 1.7 | Catalog `/Metadata` to uncompressed XMP stream (object 5), `pdfx:MSIP_Label_<guid>_*` (`Name`=Internal) | Label Internal, GUID `87ba5c36-b7cf-4793-bbc2-bd5b3a9f95ca` | Label `Internal` (GUID `87ba5c36-b7cf-4793-bbc2-bd5b3a9f95ca`) |
| `sensitivity_confidential.eml` | RFC 5322 message | Header `Sensitivity: Company-Confidential` | Text label `Company-Confidential`, no GUID | Text label `Company-Confidential` with no GUID |
| `msip_confidential.eml` | RFC 5322 message | Header `msip_labels:` with `MSIP_Label_<guid>_*` pairs (`Enabled=True`, `Name=Confidential`) | Label Confidential, GUID `9fbde396-1a24-4c79-8edf-9254a0f35055` | Label `Confidential` (GUID `9fbde396-1a24-4c79-8edf-9254a0f35055`) |
| `tlp_amber.md` | Markdown | First line `TLP:AMBER`, then a heading and two sentences | TLP marking `AMBER` | TLP `AMBER`. No MIP GUID |
| `vertraulich_stamp.txt` | Plain text | First line `VERTRAULICH – nur für den internen Gebrauch` | Text stamp, no GUID | Text stamp returned verbatim. It is not a MIP label |
| `tscp_confidential.odt` | ODT | `meta.xml`, `meta:user-defined` `urn:bails:IntellectualProperty:BusinessAuthorizationCategory:Name` (plus `...:Identifier` and `...PolicyAuthority:Name`) | Business authorization category `Confidential` | Category name `Confidential` |
| `encrypted.docx` | OLE/CFB stand-in (512 bytes) | File header `D0 CF 11 E0 A1 B1 1A E1`, then zeros. Not a ZIP | Encrypted Office container | Error "encrypted, cannot inspect" (not a classification and not a parse of a ZIP) |
| `offer-confidential.json` | JSON | None inside the content. The word "confidential" appears only in the filename | None | No label (`None`). Filename does not count as a marking |

Each file's XML parts are well-formed. The `.docx`, `.xlsx` and `.odt` files are ZIP packages with a valid `testzip()`. The ODT stores `mimetype` first and uncompressed.
